questions.question: How were the four persona briefs actually written — real user research distilled into jobs, or just demographics like age and device made up?
questions.why: Dez's brief reads as a stereotype (age, phone, one thumb) with no visible research behind the job-to-be-done framing.

questions.question: The panel said DONE on a fixed viewport and missed rotation and scrolling entirely — what exactly does the panel check, and who wrote those acceptance criteria?
questions.why: The speaker admits the panel walked a fixed viewport and still called it done on something 'pretty much unusable' the next morning.

questions.question: Now that you've seen the panel pass something broken, what's the actual workflow — does a human walk every UI change on a real device before merge, or only after a failure like this one?
questions.why: The talk ends the persona-gate story at the failure without saying what process change followed.

questions.question: Dez going from 30 seconds to 9 seconds a task is simulated, not human — what makes that a usability number at all rather than a model narrating improvement?
questions.why: The slide itself flags 'simulated, not human' but treats the number as a result anyway.

questions.question: Who on your team can decline or override what a persona panel asks for, and does that feedback ever get treated as a hard requirement instead of a signal?
questions.why: The talk gives the panel a pass/fail verdict but never says who translates its notes into design decisions.

questions.question: What did the review-screen redesign for labeling actually change on screen, and was that tested against alternatives or just shipped from the persona feedback directly?
questions.why: The 20-to-30-second review time is credited to a 'persona-driven redesign' with no detail on what changed or how it was validated.

questions.question: You call the jitter fixed once thrown-away answers hit near zero — was 'it holds' ever judged by a person watching the screen, or only by the event logs?
questions.why: The whole jitter story is told through instrumentation and replay data, never through someone's eyes on the live overlay.

questions.question: When the identify vote misses and gets a card wrong, what does the person actually see — a confident wrong answer, or something that signals uncertainty?
questions.why: The demo slide promises to show a miss but doesn't say what the failure mode looks like to the user in the moment.

questions.question: Do these persona panels ever get compared side by side against real usability sessions, or are they only ever checked against your own hands after the fact?
questions.why: The closing advice tells others to add a persona gate but the only real-user check shown is the speaker's own phone, once.

questions.question: For the 65% top-3 figure on live lots, who decided what counted as 'the right card' — the same one tapper who's judging usability elsewhere in this project?
questions.why: The bar is described as one person's own taps over five days, which is a thin evidence base for a headline accuracy number.
